reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a flash-loan method as producing up to $10,000 for free while instructing viewers to deposit BNB or liquidity and deploy and activate a contract. It claims remaining profit will return to the viewer's wallet within seconds or minutes. An educational disclaimer qualifies the presentation, and the available video evidence does not verify the contract's behavior, profitability, or any viewer loss.

citations.quote: Hack Binance Flash Loan upto $10000 For FREE
Bnb Flash loan arbitrage tutorial. Follow the flash loan attack tutorial to use the PancakeSwap exploit.
Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.
The flash loan will be paid back automatically and any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.
loan amount of 1000 that's the amount of B&B you're borrowing

opening.argument: Judge the presentation as a qualified tutorial, not a promise that every viewer will receive money. Its description says “FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY,” and the narration makes the proposed borrowing conditional on the program finding a profit. The description also discusses gas fees and the BNB needed for the contract to run. Those qualifications do not prove the method works, but they matter when deciding whether the speaker is presenting a guaranteed, cost-free payout.

citations.quote: FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY
IF this program finds a profit on Pancake Swap
Make sure you have enough BNB to pay for the token creation and flash loan contract gas fees

rebuttal.rebuttal: The headline's “FREE” claim is forceful, but the body explicitly tells viewers about costs and conditions. The quoted instruction to send liquidity establishes a required step, not by itself that the speaker will take it. Likewise, the statement that “any profit” returns to the wallet leaves open whether there will be profit. The opening rightly notes that the contract's behavior is unverified; that uncertainty also limits a conclusion about what happens to deposited funds.

citations.quote: Hack Binance Flash Loan upto $10000 For FREE

any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational disclaimer and conditional phrase do not neutralize the direct instruction to fund a newly deployed contract. The description specifies a minimum deposit and tells viewers to send liquidity to the contract, then promises an automatic repayment and rapid return of any profit. The contract's unverified behavior is a reason for caution, not evidence that the funding instruction is harmless.

opening.argument: This is organized around showing a technical workflow. The narration walks through creating a file, pasting code, selecting a compiler and deploying a contract; the sampled frames show the Remix editor and deployment interface. The speaker also describes waiting for a transaction and activating the contract in the demonstration. A viewer can evaluate this as an operational lesson with an asserted result, without treating the assertion as independently verified or assuming the lesson itself is a fraudulent solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening highlights the large headline and the requested transfer, but neither makes the on-screen walkthrough disappear. The narration describes sending funds to the newly created contract address and then running its function. That is a concrete demonstration of what the speaker says the code does; it is not independent proof of profit, but the prosecution's opening also acknowledges that the contract's behavior and any viewer loss are unverified.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Showing an editor does not establish that the pasted contract performs the advertised arbitrage or returns funds. The lesson directs viewers to obtain code from the description, send liquidity to the contract and trigger its Action function. Its narrated result is a claim about what happened, not verification of the contract's behavior. The instructional format is precisely how the funding step is conveyed.

opening.argument: The described transaction is a user-operated contract deployment, not an identified payment to the presenter. Viewers are told to use a browser wallet, deploy a new token contract and send liquidity to that new contract address. Those steps carry real financial risk, but the supplied instructions do not show a request for a password or recovery phrase, an identified presenter-controlled recipient, or a demonstrated diversion of funds. Classify what is shown: a risky proposed trading workflow, not a proven transfer to the speaker.

citations.quote: To get started, you need to have MetaMask browser extension installed.
Click transact and then confirm the gas fees to launch the token in metamask.
Under deployed contracts, copy the new token contract code.
Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies the deposit instruction and promised return. Its opening does not establish who controls the deployed contract or where deposited funds actually go. The described sequence has the viewer copy an address from the deployed contract and send liquidity there. That does not make the transaction safe, but it leaves the alleged diversion mechanism unshown; an advertised return is not evidence that one occurred.

citations.quote: Under deployed contracts, copy the new token contract code.
Go to your metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.
The flash loan will be paid back automatically and any profit will be returned to your wallet in a few seconds/minutes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A named presenter-controlled wallet or observed loss is not necessary to assess the pitch. The viewer is instructed to paste linked code, deposit a specified amount to the resulting contract and activate it, while being told that repayment and profit will follow automatically. The defense has not shown that deploying a contract makes its code trustworthy or that funds sent to it can be recovered.
